* WHEN...Until 9 PM CDT /8 PM MDT/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:

* WHERE...The following areas, Central Susitna Valley, Lower
Matanuska Valley, Southern Susitna Valley and Western Susitna
Valley.  This includes the cities of Palmer, Wasilla, Big Lake,
Skwentna, Willow, Talkeetna, Trapper Creek, And Petersville.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

August 3 through Wednesday August 5. Current estimates is for

July 21-25th event.

television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Valley West; Kuskokwim Valley East; Lime Village; Interior Kuskokwim Delta; Western Capes; Northern Alaska Peninsula; Bristol Bay Borough (Naknek and King Salmon); Northern Bristol Bay Coast; Inland Bristol Bay; Lake Iliamna / Nila Vena / Nanvarpak
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 2 at 5:05AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
A system moving in from the Bering Sea this morning will bring
widespread, prolonged rainfall for Southwest Alaska through at
least Tuesday. By Tuesday afternoon, widespread rainfall amounts
of 1 to 2 inches are expected across most of Southwest Alaska with
locally higher amounts, up to 2.5 inches possible in the Togiak
area, along the Kuskokwim Valley, and near the western Alaska
Range. Heaviest rainfall will be Sunday night into Monday for the
Kuskokwim Delta and western Bristol Bay and Monday into Tuesday
farther inland, along the western Alaska Range.

For coastal areas of the Western Capes and western Bristol Bay
(Goodnews Bay, Platinum and Togiak), southerly winds of 25 to 35
mph (sustained) will persist Sunday evening through Monday
afternoon. This could bring water levels up to 1 to 2 feet above
the mean high tide line. Winds will be strongest early Monday
morning.

Check the forecast for the latest updates, if you plan to be
outdoors.

properties.areaDesc: Central Copper Valley; Southern Copper Valley; McCarthy
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 2 at 4:41AM AKDT until August 2 at 9:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 78 to 82.

* WHERE...Central Copper Valley, McCarthy, and Southern Copper
Valley.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Daytime temperatures across the Copper River
Valley will climb to around 80 degrees today. The warmest
temperatures will be along the Edgerton Highway and McCarthy Road.
Overnight lows will drop into the lower to mid 40s, allowing for a
respite from the warm temperatures.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Young children and pets should never be left unattended in vehicles
under any circumstances as vehicle interiors can reach extreme
temperatures in as little as 10 minutes.

Take extra precautions when working in the sun. Wear sunscreen and
lightweight, loose fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous
activities to early morning or evening. Take action when you see
symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

Close curtains during the daytime to reduce sun insolation into the
home and open windows at night to allow the home to cool off.
Utilize fans or community buildings with air conditioning.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 PM AKDT THIS EVENING

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during

properties.instruction:

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 2 at 2:41AM MST until August 3 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with temperatures 101 to 106 in
Santa Cruz and Cochise counties and 107 to 112 elsewhere. Major to
Extreme HeatRisk is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Cochise County below 5000 feet, Southeast Pinal
County, Tohono O'odham Nation, Tucson Metro Area, Upper Gila River
Valley, Upper San Pedro River Valley, Upper Santa Cruz River
Valley/Altar Valley, and Western Pima County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Warm overnight low temperatures of 84 to 90
degrees in the deserts will provide little to no relief from heat
overnight. Warmest overnight low temperatures expected in the
Western Deserts.
properties.instruction:
Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

properties.areaDesc: Cook, IL; Will, IL; Lake, IN
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 2 at 4:04AM CDT until August 2 at 11:00AM CDT by NWS Chicago IL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Cook County in northeastern Illinois...
Central Will County in northeastern Illinois...
Northwestern Lake IN County in northwestern Indiana...

* WHEN...Until 1100 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Slow moving or standing
water may continue. High water may only slowly recede from flooded
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 402 AM CDT, gauges on area creeks, streams, and rivers
indicated ongoing flooding from earlier excessive rainfall in the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hammond, Gary, Tinley Park, Calumet City, Chicago Heights, East
Chicago, Lansing, Oak Forest, Harvey, Highland, Munster, Dolton,
Park Forest, Homewood, Matteson, Mokena, Frankfort, Steger, and
South Holland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means flooding is imminent or may already be
occurring. Persons along rivers, creeks, and other waterways should
take immediate precautions to protect life and property.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 11 AM CDT THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued August 2 at 6:25PM ChST until August 7 at 6:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Corrected timing information.

...SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 AM CHST
FRIDAY...

* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt and seas 8 to 12 feet expected.
Gusts to 35 kt possible.

* WHERE...Guam Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM ChST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Fresh to strong westerlies will continue
across Guam coastal waters, generating choppy seas hazardous to
small craft. Winds will peak in the first half of this week,
with a possibility of frequent gale-force gusts Monday and
Tuesday, which would necessitate a Gale Warning at that time.
Additionally, distant Typhoon Dolphin (12W) is generating a
long-period easterly swell that is moving through the Marianas,
which will gradually shift north over the next day or so, then
shift to the northwest. Meanwhile, the developing monsoon
pattern will lead to increasing southwesterly swell over the
coming days. These increasing swells and wind waves will build
combined seas to exceed 10 feet across the coastal waters,
maintaining hazardous sea conditions for much of this week.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid boating in hazardous conditions.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued August 2 at 2:52AM CDT until August 2 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM CDT /9 AM MDT/ THIS MORNING
TO 8 PM CDT /7 PM MDT/ THIS EVENING FOR MUCH OF WESTERN NORTH DAKOTA,
EXTENDING UNTIL 8 PM MDT MONDAY FOR SLOPE AND BOWMAN COUNTIES...

.Critical fire weather conditions are expected late this morning
through early this evening across much of western North Dakota. A
cold front will move into western North Dakota by early afternoon,
shifting winds from south to northwest around 20 mph with gusts up to
30 mph. Humidity is expected to fall as low as 10 to 15 percent this
afternoon. In the southwest corner of the state, humidity is only
projected to recover to around 45 percent overnight, then fall as low
as 20 percent on Monday as north winds increase to around 25 to 30
mph, with gusts as high as 40 mph. Therefore, the Red Flag Warning
remains in effect through early Monday evening for Slope and Bowman
Counties.

The National Weather Service in Bismarck ND has issued a Red Flag
Warning.

* AFFECTED AREA...Much of western North Dakota.

* TIMING...From 10 AM CDT /9 AM MDT/ this morning to 8 PM CDT /7 PM
MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...South winds shifting to the northwest around 20 mph with
gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 10 to 15 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

is moving through the Marianas, which will gradually shift north
over the next day or so, then shift to the northwest.

increasing southwesterly swell over the coming days. These
increasing swells and wind waves will build combined seas to
exceed 10 feet across the coastal waters, maintaining hazardous
sea conditions for much of this week.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 98 to
113. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Southern Gila County and portions of northern Pinal County
and eastern Maricopa County.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, Call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 1 at 11:48PM MST until August 4 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot and humid conditions. Afternoon temperatures
109 to 116. Major to Extreme Heat Risk.

* WHERE...The Phoenix metropolitan area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Increase in heat related illnesses, including heat
cramps, heat exhaustion, and heat stroke. Heat stroke can lead to
death.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, Call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued August 2 at 3:29PM ChST until August 8 at 4:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet and dangerous rip
currents expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...North and east facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 PM this evening to
4 PM ChST Saturday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through
Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Long-period east to northeast swell,
emanating from distant Typhoon Dolphin, continues to produce a
high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs, spreading to
north-facing reefs beginning tonight, with hazardous surf also
expected to develop along north and east-facing reefs tonight.
As Dolphin passes the far northern CNMI, the long-period swell
direction is expected to shift north over the next few days, and
then northwest around midweek. As it does so, a high risk of
rip currents, and hazardous surf, is expected to develop along
west facing reefs later this week.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.

able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

on Saturday and Sunday. Elevated levels of ozone are possible
throughout the northern Front Range region, with the highest
concentrations most likely in the western portions of the Front
Range.   For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:

possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, August 2, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 1 at 5:22PM PDT until August 2 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with highs 110 to 120 degrees
across the Mojave Desert. Highs 100 to 110 degrees across most of
the southern Great Basin and Arizona Strip. Little to no overnight
relief is expected, particularly in the Mojave Desert where lows of
80 to 95 degrees are forecast. This will result in Major-to-Extreme
Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
south central and southern Nevada.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM PDT /8 PM MST/ SUNDAY

* WHAT...Hot conditions expected with highs 80 to 90 degrees above
8000 feet and 90 to 105 degrees below 8000 feet. This will result
in Moderate Heat Risk.

* WHERE...In California, Eastern Sierra Slopes and White Mountains of
Inyo County. In Nevada, Sheep Range and Spring Mountains-Red Rock
Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Saturday August 01 to 400 PM Sunday August 02

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  Hot and sunny weather with light winds will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Saturday and Sunday. Elevated levels of ozone are possible
throughout the northern Front Range region, with the highest
concentrations most likely in the western portions of the Front
Range.   For Colorado air quality conditions, forecasts, and
advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Sunday, August 2, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone
pollution through state policies. For more information about
health impacts and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 1 at 1:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
As a coastal system moves across Western Alaska Sunday into
Monday, elevated water levels, widespread rain, and southerly
winds are expected across the area. Water levels could rise 1 to
3 feet above the mean high tide line in coastal areas of the
Bering and Chukchi Seas. Rain totals from Sunday afternoon
through early Tuesday morning are expected to range from 1 to 2
inches south of the Bering Strait and from 0.5 to 1 inch north of
the Bering Strait. From Sunday afternoon through Tuesday night,
southerly winds could gust to 30 to 40 mph, with gusts over 40 mph
possible over the YK Delta. Those in coastal areas should take
extra precautions to ensure that belongings are properly secured
ahead of these increasing winds and water levels.

Monday, it will bring widespread rain and southerly winds across
the area. Rain totals from Sunday afternoon through early Tuesday
morning are expected range from 1 to 2 inches across most of the

although no flooding is expected. From Sunday afternoon through
Tuesday night, southerly winds could gust as high as 40 mph in the
Lower Yukon and Upper Kuskokwim Valleys, with gusts over 30 mph
possible elsewhere.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 1 at 2:18PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke.

Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...Clearwater and Idaho Counties.

* WHEN...Until noon PDT August 3, 2026.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is less likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Lewiston Regional Office at (208) 799-4370

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 1 at 2:56PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
AQAHGX

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued an
Ozone Action Day for the Houston, Galveston, and Brazoria area for
Sunday, August 2, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone pollution in the Houston, Galveston, and
surrounding areas on Sunday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by
sharing a ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive through lanes, conserving energy and keeping your vehicle
properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:
Ozone: The Facts www.tceq.texas.gov/airquality/monops/ozonefacts.html
EPA AirNow: www.airnow.gov/?city=Houston&state=TX&country=USA
Take Care of Texas:
www.takecareoftexas.org/conservation-tips/keep-our-air-clean

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:

the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

* WHAT...Temperatures of 100 to 106 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Little Colorado River Valley and the lower elevations of
Navajo Nation in Arizona; including the Kaibito Plateau, Painted
Desert, and Chinle Valley.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST /9 PM MDT/ Monday.

* IMPACTS...Pets, livestock, and those sensitive to heat, such as the
homeless, elderly, and children will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses. Those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration will be at the greatest risk.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.
Anyone overcome by heat should be moved to a cool and shaded
location. Heat stroke is an emergency! Call 9 1 1.

NWSheadline: HEAT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MST /9 PM MDT/ MONDAY

properties.areaDesc: Grand Canyon Country
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued August 1 at 11:27AM MST until August 4 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions expected below 4000 feet, with
daytime temperatures ranging from 103 to 108 degrees at Havasupai
Gardens, and 111 to 115 degrees at Phantom Ranch.

* WHERE...Lower elevations of the Grand Canyon.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Most individuals will be at risk for heat-related
illnesses without effective cooling or adequate hydration,
especially with prolonged outdoor exposure.
properties.instruction:
This warning is reserved for only the hottest days of the year and is
issued when temperatures are expected to rise to dangerous levels.

Day hikers on Bright Angel Trail should descend no farther than 1 1/2
miles from the upper trailhead. Between the hours of 10 AM and 4 PM,
hikers should be out of the canyon or at Havasupai Gardens or Bright
Angel campgrounds, physical activity is discouraged. All hikers
should have adequate gear, including a wide-brimmed hat, sunscreen,
salty snacks, sufficient water, and electrolyte mix. Doubling your
calorie intake helps maintain your energy.

Hike smart.

NWSheadline: EXTREME HEAT WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 PM MST TUESDAY BELOW 4000 FEET

* WHERE...A portion of west central Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Citrus, Coastal Hernando, Coastal Levy, Inland
Citrus, Inland Hernando and Inland Levy.

* WHEN...From noon EDT today through Monday evening.

creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

combined with a frontal boundary will create the potential
for periods of widespread showers and thunderstorms with
locally heavy rain through Monday.

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Ada, ID; Adams, ID; Canyon, ID; Gem, ID; Owyhee, ID; Payette, ID; Washington, ID
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 31 at 3:03PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality.

Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...Ada, Adams, Canyon, Gem, Owyhee, Payette, and Washington
Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 2 PM MDT MONDAY.

* IMPACTS...Members of sensitive groups may experience health
effects. The general public is not likely to be affected.
properties.instruction:
Air pollutants can cause breathing difficulties for children, the
elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

THIS STATEMENT IS ISSUED BY THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY, AIR QUALITY GROUP FOR MORE INFORMATION, CONTACT DEQ's
Boise Regional Office at (208) 373-0550
Twin Falls Regional Office at (208) 736-2190
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY FOR Ada, Adams, Canyon, Gem, Owyhee, Payette, and Washington Counties

properties.areaDesc: Baker, OR; Harney, OR; Malheur, OR
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 31 at 3:03PM MDT by NWS Boise ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...High concentration of smoke particulates from wildfires

* WHERE...Baker, Harney, and northern Malheur Counties.

* WHEN...UNTIL 2 PM PDT MONDAY.

* IMPACTS...Smoke can irritate the eyes, lungs and worsen some
medical conditions. People most at risk to adverse health effects
include infants, young children, people with heart or lung
disease, older adults, and pregnant women.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on
weather. Check current conditions on the Oregon Smoke Information
Blog, DEQ's Air Quality Index, or by downloading the free
OregonAIR app on your smartphone.
properties.instruction:
* Stay inside if possible. Keep windows and doors closed.

* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity.

* Use high efficiency particulate air (HEPA) filters in indoor
ventilation systems or portable air purifiers.

* Be aware of smoke in your area and avoid places with the highest
levels.

* If you have heart or lung disease, or asthma, follow your
healthcare provider's advice.

For current Oregon air quality conditions, please visit:
https://aqi.oregon.gov

For additional information, please visit:
https://www.oregon.gov/deq
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

Washington Department of Ecology
Colville Confederated Tribes
Environmental Protection Agency
Spokane Regional Clean Air Agency

Ferry, Okanogan, Pend Oreille, and Stevens Counties until further
notice due to current and expected wildfire smoke from regional
fires. Extremely critical fire weather Saturday will produce
significant smoke from ongoing and emerging fires. Particulate matter

areas downwind from active wildfires in Washington, Oregon, and
British Columbia.

from ongoing and emerging fires. Shifting winds will likely bring
smoke into these counties beginning Saturday evening. PM2.5 may reach
unhealthy levels.

for cleaner indoor air.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued July 30 at 4:02PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has issued an air quality alert due to
harmful levels of ozone pollution. Visit
https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted air
quality levels.

* WHERE...Glendora, San Fernando Valley, Santa Clarita Valley, San
Gabriel Valley, San Bernardino, Redlands, Riverside, Crestline and
the Coachella Valley.. Levels of ozone pollution can vary by time
and location depending on emissions and air pollution transport.

* WHEN...until 8 PM Sunday. The highest ozone levels typically occur
in the afternoon and early-evening hours.

* IMPACTS... Ozone air pollution can cause serious health problems,
including trouble breathing, asthma attacks, and lung damage.
Everyone can be affected, but sensitive groups such as people with
lung disease, older adults, people who are pregnant, children, and
those who spend a lot of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, and grilling

To help minimize outdoor ozone air pollution levels:

* Limit the use of gasoline powered lawn and garden equipment
until evening hours
* Try to delay trips to the gas station and the use of household
chemicals until the evening
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.
